exercises.name: Two-Hand Kettlebell Swing
cues: Hike the bell back between the legs
Snap the hips to float the bell to chest height
Arms stay relaxed, ribs down
exercises.description: Hip-hinge ballistic movement; the foundational kettlebell exercise.

exercises.name: One-Hand Kettlebell Swing
cues: Grip the handle at a slight angle
Resist the bell twisting your torso
Free arm mirrors the working arm
exercises.description: Swing driven by one arm; adds an anti-rotation demand on the core.

exercises.name: Hand-to-Hand Swing
cues: Release and catch at the top float
Soft grip, quiet hand
Keep the hinge rhythm unbroken
exercises.description: Swing where the bell is passed between hands at the top of each rep.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean
cues: Zip the bell up close to the body
Spear the hand through, don't catch on the wrist
Land soft in the rack position
exercises.description: Brings the bell from the floor or a swing to the racked position on the shoulder.

exercises.name: Clean & Press
cues: Clean to the rack, pause and breathe
Press with the whole body braced
Lock out with the biceps by the ear
exercises.description: A clean into an overhead press; a complete strength movement in one rep.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Strict Press
cues: Brace the ribs down before pressing
Drive the bell slightly back as it passes the head
Squeeze the glute on the pressing side
exercises.description: Overhead press from the rack with no leg drive.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Push Press
cues: Short dip with vertical torso
Drive through the legs, then punch up
Lock out overhead before lowering
exercises.description: Overhead press assisted by a sharp dip and drive from the legs.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Snatch
cues: High-pull path, then punch the hand up
Bell rotates around the wrist, no flop
One smooth arc from hips to overhead
exercises.description: Explosive movement taking the bell from between the legs to overhead in one motion.

exercises.name: Kettlebell High Pull
cues: Hinge and hike like a swing
Lead with the elbow, high and wide
Bell stays close, knuckles to the chin
exercises.description: A swing that finishes with a hard row to chin height; snatch progression.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
cues: Hold the bell by the horns at the chest
Sit straight down, elbows inside the knees
Drive the floor away, ribs stacked over hips
exercises.description: Squat holding a single bell at the chest; great for depth and posture.

exercises.name: Double Front Squat
cues: Both bells racked, elbows down and in
Big breath and brace before descending
Keep the chest tall against the load
exercises.description: Squat with two bells in the rack position; heavy lower-body strength.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Reverse Lunge
cues: Step straight back, knee to a soft touch
Torso stays upright
Push through the front heel to stand
exercises.description: Step-back lunge; loaded in the rack, goblet, or suitcase position.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Walking Lunge
cues: Long steps, tall spine
Trail knee tracks down, not forward
Even tempo, no rushing the turnaround
exercises.description: Lunges travelling forward; carry position dictates the core demand.

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
cues: Eyes on the bell until standing
Roll to elbow, to hand, sweep the leg
Reverse the steps exactly on the way down
exercises.description: A slow floor-to-standing sequence under load; shoulder stability and control.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Halo
cues: Hold the bell upside down by the horns
Circle tight around the head
Ribs stay down, hips still
exercises.description: Bell circled around the head; shoulder mobility and warm-up staple.

exercises.name: Around the World
cues: Pass the bell hand-to-hand behind the back and front
Stand tall, brace the trunk
Switch direction halfway through
exercises.description: Bell passed in a circle around the body; grip and bracing warm-up.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Deadlift
cues: Bell between the heels, hinge to reach it
Long spine, pull the slack out
Stand by squeezing the glutes
exercises.description: Hinge to lift the bell from the floor; teaches the swing pattern slowly.

exercises.name: Suitcase Deadlift
cues: Bell beside the foot, like a suitcase
Don't let the torso tip toward the bell
Shoulders and hips stay level
exercises.description: Single-sided deadlift; strong anti-lateral-flexion core challenge.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Bent-Over Row
cues: Hinge to a flat back, free hand on the thigh
Row the bell to the hip, elbow past the ribs
Control the lower, no torso twist
exercises.description: Single-arm row from a hinged position; upper-back pulling strength.

exercises.name: Gorilla Row
cues: Two bells between the feet, wide hinge stance
Row one while the other stays planted
Fight the rotation with the braced side
exercises.description: Alternating rows off the floor with two bells; pull volume plus anti-rotation.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
cues: Stand tall, shoulders packed
Short quick steps, quiet feet
Don't let the bells swing
exercises.description: Walk carrying a bell in each hand; grip, posture, and trunk endurance.

exercises.name: Rack Carry
cues: Bell racked, elbow tight to the ribs
Resist leaning away from the load
Breathe behind the brace
exercises.description: Carry with the bell in the rack position; offset load, heavy core demand.

exercises.name: Overhead Carry
cues: Lock the elbow, biceps by the ear
Wrist stacked over shoulder over hip
Ribs down, glutes on
exercises.description: Carry with the bell locked out overhead; shoulder stability under fatigue.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Windmill
cues: Bell locked overhead, eyes on it
Push the hip out, hinge sideways
Reach the free hand down a straight front leg
exercises.description: Side-bending hinge under an overhead load; hip and thoracic mobility.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Russian Twist
cues: Sit tall, lean back to a strong brace
Rotate from the ribs, not just the arms
Tap the bell each side, heels light or lifted
exercises.description: Seated rotational core exercise holding the bell at the chest.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Pull-Through
cues: High plank, feet wide for a base
Reach under and drag the bell across
Hips stay square to the floor
exercises.description: From a plank, drag the bell side to side; hard anti-rotation hold.

exercises.name: Deck Squat
cues: Roll back holding the bell at the chest
Rock forward, plant the feet, stand up
Use momentum, not a jerk
exercises.description: Roll back to the floor and back up to a stand; conditioning and mobility.

exercises.name: Push-Up
cues: Hands under the shoulders, body in one straight line
Elbows track back at roughly 45 degrees
Ribs down, squeeze the glutes — no sagging hips
exercises.description: Horizontal press against your own bodyweight; the staple upper-body push.

exercises.name: Knee Push-Up
cues: Knees down, hips in line with the shoulders
Same elbow path as a full push-up
Lower under control rather than dropping
exercises.description: Push-up with the knees down to shorten the lever; the honest way to build the full version.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
cues: Hips high, body in an inverted V
Lower the crown of the head toward the floor
Keep the weight over the hands, not the feet
exercises.description: Hips-high push-up that tips the load onto the shoulders — the bodyweight overhead press.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
cues: Feet about shoulder width, toes slightly out
Sit down between the hips, chest tall
Drive the floor away and stand all the way up
exercises.description: The foundational squat pattern with no load — a warm-up, a filler, or a whole workout at volume.

exercises.name: Jump Squat
cues: Dip to a quarter squat, then jump
Land quietly through the whole foot
Absorb into the next rep rather than bouncing
exercises.description: Explosive squat that leaves the floor; adds power and a heart rate to the squat pattern.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
cues: Back flat to the wall, thighs parallel to the floor
Knees stacked over the ankles
Breathe — the urge is to hold your breath
exercises.description: Isometric squat held against a wall; burns without any impact on the knees.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
cues: Step back and lower the back knee toward the floor
Front shin close to vertical
Push through the front heel to stand
exercises.description: Stepping back rather than forward keeps the front knee quiet; the friendliest single-leg start.

exercises.name: Split Squat
cues: Set a long stance and stay there for all the reps
Drop straight down, not forward
Keep the torso upright
exercises.description: A lunge held in place — all the single-leg work with none of the stepping.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
cues: Heels close to the hips, toes light
Drive through the heels and squeeze at the top
Ribs down — don't arch the lower back
exercises.description: Floor-based hip extension; wakes the glutes up without asking anything of the spine.

exercises.name: Sit-Up
cues: Feet anchored or flat, knees bent
Peel the spine off the floor one vertebra at a time
Lower with the same control you came up with
exercises.description: Full-range trunk flexion from the floor; the classic, and still a good one.

exercises.name: Crunch
cues: Lift only the shoulder blades off the floor
Chin off the chest, eyes to the ceiling
Hands rest by the head — don't pull on the neck
exercises.description: Short-range trunk flexion; less hip flexor than a sit-up, and kinder to the lower back.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
cues: Opposite elbow toward opposite knee
Extend the free leg long and low
Slow down — speed hides the work
exercises.description: Alternating crunch with rotation; brings the obliques into the pattern.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
cues: Press the lower back into the floor and keep it there
Legs straight, lower only as far as you can hold that
Hands under the hips if the back lifts
exercises.description: Lower-abdominal work; the range is only as long as your back stays flat.

exercises.name: Plank
cues: Elbows under the shoulders, forearms flat
One line from heels to head
Squeeze the glutes and tuck the ribs
exercises.description: Isometric anti-extension hold; the baseline test of whether the trunk can stay stiff.

exercises.name: Side Plank
cues: Elbow under the shoulder, feet stacked or staggered
Push the hip to the ceiling
Don't let the top shoulder roll forward
exercises.description: Isometric hold on one side; the anti-lateral-flexion counterpart to the plank.

exercises.name: Hollow Hold
cues: Lower back pinned to the floor throughout
Arms and legs long, shoulders just off the ground
Raise the limbs higher if the back lifts
exercises.description: Gymnastic hollow position; teaches the trunk to hold a shape under load.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
cues: Opposite arm and leg extend together
Lower back stays flat on the floor
Move slowly and breathe out as you extend
exercises.description: Anti-extension drill done lying down; hard to cheat and easy on the back.

exercises.name: Superman
cues: Face down, arms and legs lifted
Reach long rather than lifting high
Look at the floor to keep the neck neutral
exercises.description: Prone spinal extension; the counterweight to a day spent sitting.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber
cues: Strong plank first, then drive the knees
Hips stay level — no bouncing
Hands stacked under the shoulders
exercises.description: A plank with moving legs; conditioning that keeps the trunk honest.

exercises.name: Jumping Jack
cues: Land soft through the balls of the feet
Arms all the way overhead
Find a rhythm and hold it
exercises.description: The universal warm-up; raises the heart rate and needs no space at all.

exercises.name: High Knees
cues: Knees to hip height
Stay tall — don't lean back
Quick feet, light contacts
exercises.description: Running on the spot with intent; a fast way to raise the heart rate in one square metre.

exercises.name: Burpee
cues: Hands down, feet back to a plank
Chest to the floor if you want the full version
Jump the feet in and stand tall
exercises.description: Squat, plank, push, jump — the whole body in one rep, and the reason everyone dreads it.

exercises.name: Inchworm
cues: Hinge and walk the hands out to a plank
Keep the legs as straight as your hamstrings allow
Walk the feet back to the hands
exercises.description: Walking hand-to-foot stretch; a warm-up that opens the hamstrings and loads the trunk.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
cues: Knees an inch off the floor and keep them there
Opposite hand and foot move together
Hips low and level — no swaying
exercises.description: Quadrupedal crawl with the knees hovering; deceptively hard on the trunk and shoulders.
